title: Planner: Planner Agent in group-based basic plans
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documentation supports the Planner PowerShell controls, their security-group behaviour and the Copilot licence requirement. The default and a separate feature-specific price or meter remain undocumented; two small checklist corrections would improve the governance instructions.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A separate price specific to Planner Agent in basic plans is not published in the cited product documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner Agent basic plans pricing meter Copilot Credits license. Read Planner service description, turn-off-planner-agent, planner-for-admins and release notes. These specify Copilot entitlement but no separate basic-plan Agent price; results for Studio and Cowork concern different products.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A meter specific to Planner Agent in basic plans is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner Agent basic plans pricing meter Copilot Credits license. Read Planner service description and turn-off-planner-agent. The service description notes metered Graph APIs, not a Planner Agent meter; search excerpts for Studio and Cowork billing do not describe this feature.

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for the Planner Agent tenant-wide on/off policy in Planner.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner Agent AllowPlannerCopilot default enabled admin center UI restrict security group; Planner Agent PlannerCopilotAllowedGroupId admin UI security group Microsoft 365 admin center. Read turn-off-planner-agent and manage-copilot-agents-integrated-apps; no UI for the Planner policy.

claims.claim: Set-PlannerConfiguration -AllowPlannerCopilot $false turns off Planner Agent for all users.
claims.quote: To turn off Planner Agent and Planner Agent chat for all users: Set-PlannerConfiguration -AllowPlannerCopilot $false

claims.claim: With PlannerCopilotAllowedGroupId set to $null, AllowPlannerCopilot $true turns Planner Agent on for all users.
No admin UI is documented for setting the Planner Agent allowed security group in Planner.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner Agent PlannerCopilotAllowedGroupId admin UI security group Microsoft 365 admin center. Read turn-off-planner-agent and manage-copilot-agents-integrated-apps; group selection for this Planner policy is documented in PowerShell, not UI. Cowork plugin controls are a different experience.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-PlannerConfiguration -AllowPlannerCopilot $true -PlannerCopilotAllowedGroupId <security group id> restricts Planner Agent to the specified security group.
claims.quote: To turn on Planner Agent and Planner Agent chat for a specific security group: Set-PlannerConfiguration -AllowPlannerCopilot $true -PlannerCopilotAllowedGroupId <security group id>

claims.claim: Members of nested groups are included in the allowed security-group scope.
claims.quote: Users who are members of the specified security group, including those in nested groups, will have access.

claims.claim: An invalid security group ID disables access for all users even when AllowPlannerCopilot is $true.
claims.quote: If the Security Group ID is invalid, no users will have access, even if AllowPlannerCopilot is set to $true.

claims.claim: User licence assignment is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns the specified licence to the user.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Licence assignment requires at least a License or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.quote: To verify your settings, run the following command: Get-PlannerConfiguration. AllowPlannerCopilot: True or False; PlannerCopilotAllowedGroupId: Displays the Security Group ID when these features are turned on for your organization

claims.claim: The Planner PowerShell instructions apply to task execution and status reporting in both basic and premium plans.

claims.claim: The allowed security-group ID must correspond to an existing group in Microsoft Entra ID.
